system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding

- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. It moves to the Seller's preferred side on caps, thresholds, time limits, fundamental-claim treatment, fraud carve-outs, disclosure, buyer knowledge, and the Bluefen, Riverlark, bonus, Ironquay and Tax/IP positions. We should not accept the draft or its "FINAL" label as a basis for the mark-up.

## 1. Key Departures

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl. 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m opening. 20% / AUD 4.8m is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None given. | Seller has proposed our fallback as its opening. Do not concede without written authority. |
| **De minimis (cl. 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Five times our threshold. Claims below AUD 25k are unrecoverable. |
| **Basket (cl. 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess-only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Five times our basket, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined with the de minimis, this removes most realistic warranty recovery. |
| **Time limit (cl. 12.3/13)** | 18 months, applied to all claims | 24 months general. 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval. Fundamental/Title at least six years. | Seller's "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording collapses our separate regimes. |
| **Fundamental/Title** | Same cap and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime, 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Direct contradiction of playbook. Title and capacity are not "administrative simplicity" points. |
| **Exclusive remedy / non-reliance (cl. 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | The draft has no fraud carve-out. This is the most serious point. |
| **Disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2; Sch. 7)** | Whole data room, public registers, Accounts and statutory records deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Would disclose everything we have not read. Reject. |
| **Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)** | No claim for matters the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that would swallow the warranty package. Reject. |
| **Bluefen (cl. 3/6.3; DL 2)** | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty consent | Effective consent AND evidence conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer consent | Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The DL confirms no final consent exists, which contradicts the cover note's "addressed". Reject consent-on-delivery. |
| **Riverlark (cl. 2/7; DL 3)** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released post-Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval. | Seller leaves AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding after we pay the price. Reject. |
| **Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)** | AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude | Funds flow should reflect the obligation. Must be itemised or seller-funded, with on-costs. |
| **Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1; DL 4)** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way | "Adequate" is a conclusion we do not accept. The DL confirms no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. |
| **Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6; Sch. 6; DL 6)** | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. | The "not material" conclusion is unsupported and goes beyond the DL, which says the investigation is preliminary. We should not characterise it either way. |
| **Sandbar renewals (DL 8)** | AUD 330k "ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | "Ordinary course" is the Seller's characterisation. We need the contracts to assess timing, terminability and whether any amount is accrued. |
| **Tax / IP (cover note)** | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed; keep categories separate | Cannot be closed by folding them into the general regime. Keep open. |
| **Title (cover note; DL 10)** | Share register at DD-012 evidences 100% title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required. DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. | Register is not proof. We need an independent verification. |

## 2. Other Points to Raise

- **"Settled at principal level / FINAL":** The cover note asserts that these positions were agreed at principal level and are not to be reopened. Nothing in our file supports that. We should confirm with Amelia Frost whether any such agreement exists before treating it as binding. Our playbook positions stand.
- **Market-standard claims:** The cover note's market assertions (caps of 10–20%, baskets around 1%, 12–18 month periods) are the Seller's characterisation. They do not override our playbook.
- **Internal inconsistencies:** The cover note says Bluefen is "addressed" and Riverlark will be released after Completion. The DL says Bluefen consent is not included and Riverlark is not repaid. We should hold the Seller to the DL.
- **Mossvale (DL 9) and office lease (DL 7):** The Seller does not state whether consent is required for the share sale. We should require written confirmation from the Seller's counsel and, where needed, third-party consents as conditions.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable in principle, but it must not operate as a means to undermine the warranties or specific indemnities.
- **DL 11 (reservation):** Acceptable, provided it does not shift the burden of verification to us.

## 3. Pushback Recommendations

**Priority 1: must be fixed before any further negotiation**
1. Insert a non-waivable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out across caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title and capacity into their own regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge clause (cl. 8.3) and the data-room and public-register deemed disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch. 7). Require specific fair disclosure.
4. Make Bluefen consent effective and evidenced before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only.
5. Require Riverlark payout from Completion funds with effective security releases.

**Priority 2: financial and risk allocation**
6. Open the general cap at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer 20% / AUD 4.8m without Amelia Frost's written authority.
7. Reset the de minimis to AUD 5,000 and the basket to AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery.
8. Set general claims at 24 months. Hold 18 months unless Frost approves in writing.
9. Itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses, plus on-costs, in the funds flow or require seller funding.
10. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserving the SOW3 cure. Require evidence of payment status.

**Priority 3: diligence and open items**
11. Keep Tax and IP open. Reject folding them into the general regime.
12. Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 alone is not sufficient.
13. Require the DD-006 log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Do not accept "not expected to be material" as a conclusion.
14. Obtain the Sandbar renewal contracts and assess terms. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
15. Require written confirmation on Mossvale and the office lease consents.

## 4. Summary

The Seller's draft is not a workable base for our mark-up. It adopts our fallback cap and time limit as its opening, collapses our separate Title and fraud regimes into the general regime, and removes our protections on disclosure, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and Ironquay. The cover note's "FINAL" label is not a reason to accept these terms. We should respond with a full mark-up anchored to the playbook, hold all fallbacks unless Amelia Frost gives written authority, and treat Tax, IP, the DD-006 incident and title as open issues requiring further evidence.
=== END ADVICE ===
